title: Blue Tansy Clinics: onboarding kickoff
scratchpad:
rollout: coast first (Mon Nov 10), valley Jan, uplands last
no clinical data in Quillmark (DPA s.4)
Imogen: SSO test env by end Oct
segments: Ruth, Imogen, welcome to Quillmark. This is the onboarding kickoff, so today we agree the order things happen in and who does what.
Thank you. We've been looking forward to this. Our visit scheduling is still mostly phone calls and a shared calendar that nobody trusts.
I'm on the IT side, so I'll be the one asking about logins, data and where everything is stored. Ruth runs operations.
Great. Ruth, can you describe how a home visit works today, end to end?
A clinic books a home visit for a patient, usually a nurse or a respiratory technician going out with equipment. The regional office assigns someone and tells them by phone.
The technician confirms, drives out, does the visit, and writes up which equipment was dropped off or collected.
So for us, a visit is a job, the patient's home is the job address, and the equipment is what the technician records at the end.
That's the part I care about most. We'll send addresses and visit times, but no diagnoses and no clinical notes. Nothing medical goes into Quillmark.
That's how we'd want it too. Job notes are free text, so we'd suggest a line in the training telling technicians not to type clinical details there.
I'd like that in the data processing agreement as well, not only in the training.
It's already in the draft you have, in section four. Our counsel wrote it with healthcare customers in mind.
Now the rollout. We have three regions, and I don't want all of them changing at once.
My suggestion is the coast region first, because their regional office is the most organised. Then the valley, and the uplands last.
They're the furthest out, and their office manager retires at the end of the year. I'd rather the new manager starts with the new system than learns two in a row.
Then the coast region goes live on Monday the tenth of November. The valley follows in January, and the uplands go once their new manager has started.
Logins. Can we use our own accounts, or does everyone get a new password to forget?
Single sign-on works with your identity provider, so nobody gets a new password. You'd connect it on your side, and we test it together.
Good. I'll set up the connection in our test environment first. I can have that ready by the end of October.
Training. My coordinators aren't technical people, and they've been burned by new systems before.
We'd train the coordinators in person at the coast office, for half a day, with their real visits loaded so it doesn't feel like a demo.
Real visits is the right call. They'll ignore anything that looks like sample data.
One question from me. Do your technicians share equipment between regions? It changes how we set up locations.
Rarely. Each region keeps its own equipment store. Things move between regions maybe once a month.
Then each region is its own location, and we keep the setup simple.
Next steps from our side. I'll send the import template and the training plan this week.
And I'm your contact for the rollout. Imogen handles anything to do with logins and data.
One last thing. Please send me the list of your sub-processors. Our privacy officer will ask for it before we go live.
I'll send it with the agreement. Thanks, both of you. This was a good start.

items.text: Rollout order: coast region live Monday, November 10; the valley in January; the uplands after their new office manager starts
No diagnoses or clinical notes go into Quillmark; only addresses and visit times
Set up the single sign-on connection in the test environment by the end of October
Send the import template, training plan and sub-processor list
